key_insight: The paper extends a Boltzmann-based discontinuous Galerkin solver with an arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian formulation to accurately handle nearly incompressible flows with moving boundaries.
engineering_relevance: It enables high-order simulation of complex moving-mesh aerodynamics on unstructured grids, which is useful for flapping foils, morphing bodies, and fluid-structure interaction problems.
method: Maps the continuous Boltzmann equations to a reference frame to account for mesh motion via an added advection term.
Discretizes the ALE Boltzmann system with high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods on unstructured meshes.
Uses a semi-analytic Runge-Kutta time integrator and consistent geometric-factor updates to satisfy the geometric conservation law.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on free-stream preservation, a moving Taylor-Green vortex, and showcased on a plunging airfoil and a moving 3D carangiform fish with perfectly matched layers.
watch_item: GPU-accelerated ALE DG implementations can be sensitive to geometric update consistency and boundary-motion complexity, especially in three-dimensional moving-mesh setups.
paper_title: A High-Order Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian Discontinuous Galerkin Method for the Boltzmann Equation in Nearly Incompressible Flows
